brief: A two-storey garage tower sturdy enough that it will never wobble or crack with tins of screws in it.

requirements.evidence: 6x full bases: piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:0,1,0;full at level 0 and piece:0,0,1;full, piece:0,1,1;full, piece:1,0,1;full at level 1, joined with snaps and joint bolts
3x storage bins on top storey (bin:0,0,1, bin:0,1,1 div3 + bin:1,0,1 div2) filled with 8x heap-screws props visible from above
requirements.requirement: Garage storage for tins of screws / small hardware

requirements.evidence: Snaps on all 3 ground cells, joint bolts on all touching walls both storeys, capOpenFaces + lockJoints applied; but parts are 3D-printed plastic in user-chosen material and configurator checks fit/collisions only — no load, wobble or crack guarantee can be given
requirements.requirement: Sturdy enough that it will never wobble or crack with tins of screws in it

finish.summary: Built a compact 3-cell x 2-storey tower with divided bins holding screws, fully snapped, joint-bolted, capped and locked. Shape helps stiffness but absolute never-wobble/crack guarantee is not possible — strength depends on user-chosen print material.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Raising your two-storey garage tower — sturdy shape, honest limits on load.
